sentences.text: ORDER This application is filed by the cross objector/claimant to condone the delay of 3971 days in filing the cross objection.
The cross objection is filed by the claimant dissatisfied with the quantum of compensation awarded by the tribunal in O.P(MV) No.1533 of 2001 passed by the Motor Accidents Claims tribunal, Palakkad.

2. In the application for condonation of delay, it is stated that the cross objector was a minor aged 13 years at the time of accident and that he became totally paraplegic and his lower limbs became unfunctional.

As stated in the affidavit, the applicant ought to have filed the cross objection on or before 2025:KER:93315 C.M.APPL.NO.2/2025 IN C.O. 71 OF 2025 30.11.2014, since the notice of the appeal was served on him on 29.04.2014.
It is also stated that after the accident, he was confined to a wheelchair and was deprived of further education and other possibilities in life.
The entire proceedings were prosecuted by his father, who passed away in the year 2024.
His mother, being illiterate and struggling with serious health issues, is incapable of taking care of the applicant as well.
It is also stated that after the accident, the father was in a state of depression and he had shown withdrawal symptoms.

The applicant contends that the delay was not deliberate; but due to poverty,
physical incapacity, lack of legal knowledge and dependency.

sentences.text: The first respondent insurance company filed a counter affidavit stating that no proper reason has been stated for condoning the delay in filing the cross objection.
There has been negligence and laches on the part of the petitioner in preferring this belated cross objection.

It is also contended that 2025:KER:93315 C.M.APPL.NO.2/2025 IN C.O. 71 OF 2025 the belated cross objection is filed in order to claim the benefits based on the subsequent decisions of the apex court, which is not permitted under law.

It is further contended that his father was alive till 2024 and there was callous indifference and negligence on the part of the cross objector in preferring this belated cross objection and sought for dismissal of the application.
4. I have heard the learned counsel appearing for the cross objector and the learned standing counsel appearing for the insurance company.
5. Admittedly, the appeal was filed by the insurer in the year 2014 and the notice was served on the cross objector/claimant on 29.04.2014
Accordingly, the cross objection ought to have been filed on or before 30.11.2014.
The vakalath was filed for the claimant/respondent on 14.12.2014 itself.
After receipt of notice of appeal, they thought it proper not to file any appeal, since the amount awarded was found by 2025:KER:93315 C.M.APPL.NO.2/2025 IN C.O. 71 OF 2025 them to be satisfactory.
It is stated that the cross objector was a minor aged 13 years at the time of accident and that now the cross objector is 37 years old.
As per the affidavit, the condition of the cross objector is very pathetic.

Though it is stated that after the accident, the father of the cross-objector fell into a state of depression and showed withdrawal symptoms, the affidavit fails to provide any satisfactory explanation for the delay in filing the cross-objection from 2014 to 2024.
In the affidavit, it is stated when the counsel enquired about the health condition of the cross-objector in 2024, he fervently requested and sought enhancement of the compensation.

6. In Esha Bhattacharjee v. Raghunathpur Nafar Academy [(2013) 12 SCC 649], the apex court held that there is a distinction between an inordinate delay and a delay of short duration, for to the former, the doctrine of prejudice is attracted, whereas to the latter, it may not be applicable.

entities.text: Esha Bhattacharjee v. Raghunathpur Nafar Academy [(2013) 12 SCC 649]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: That apart, the first one warrants a strict approach, whereas the 2025:KER:93315 C.M.APPL.NO.2/2025 IN C.O. 71 OF 2025 second calls for liberal delineation.

7. In Majji Sannemma v. Reddy Sridevi and Ors. (2021 KHC 6863), the apex court held as follows:
".....the discretion to condone the delay has to be exercised judiciously based on facts and circumstances of each case.

entities.text: Majji Sannemma v. Reddy Sridevi and Ors. (2021 KHC 6863)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is further observed that the expression "sufficient cause" cannot be liberally interpreted if negligence, inaction or lack of bona fides is attributed to the party.
It is further observed that even though limitation may harshly affect rights of a party but it has to be applied with all its rigour when prescribed by statute.

It is further held that in case a party has acted with negligence, lack of bona fides or there is inaction then there cannot be any justified ground for condoning the delay even by imposing conditions.
Each application for condonation of delay has to be decided within the 2025:KER:93315 C.M.APPL.NO.2/2025 IN C.O. 71 OF 2025 framework laid down by this Court.

It is further observed that if courts start condoning delay where no sufficient cause is made out by imposing conditions then Ratheesh vs The National Insurance Company Ltd on 4 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/140176313/
3 that would amount to violation of statutory principles and showing utter disregard to legislature."
8.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In Thirunagalingam v. Lingeswaran [2025 KHC OnLine 6470], it is held by the apex court that the delay should not be condoned merely as an act of generosity.
Pursuit of substantial justice must not come at the cost of causing prejudice to the opposing party.

In Pathapati Subba Reddy (died) By L.Rs. v. Special Deputy Collector (LA) [2024 KHC OnLine 6197], the apex court held that the discretionary power of Court in condoning delay, ought to admit the appeal preferred after the expiry of time is discretionary in nature and may not be exercised even sufficient cause is shown based upon host of other factors such as negligence, failure to exercise due 2025:KER:93315 C.M.APPL.NO.2/2025 IN C.O. 71 OF 2025 diligence etc.

entities.text: Pathapati Subba Reddy (died) By L.Rs. v. Special Deputy Collector (LA) [2024 KHC OnLine 6197]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In Pathapati Subba Reddy (supra), it was further held that, in the light of the public policy upon which law of limitation is based, the object behind the law of limitation and mandatory and directory nature of Section 3 and Section 5 that we have to examine and strike a balance between Section 3 and Section 5 in the matters of condoning the delay.
9. In the present case, the cross objector was represented by his father and it is only in 2024 that his father expired.

Of course, the motor vehicles act is a benevolent legislature, but its beneficial nature does not justify condoning inordinate delay in filing the cross objection, especially after the parties have appeared through their counsel.

In Majjii Sannemma (supra), it is observed by the apex Court that if court starts condoning delay, there is no sufficient cause made out by imposing conditions,
then that would amount to violation of statutory principles and showing utter discard to legislature.
In the present case, there is a delay of more than ten years in filing the cross objection.
The reasons stated by the cross objector are not satisfactory.

Accordingly, the C.M.Application for condoning the delay of 3971 days in filing in the cross objection stands dismissed Sd/-

The above cross objection is filed by the claimant aggrieved by the inadequate compensation awarded in O.P. (MV) No.1533 of 2001 passed by the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Palakkad.
Since the C.M.Application for condoning the delay in filing the cross objection is dismissed, the cross objection is also dismissed.
